Wage growth has not kept pace with a resurgence in inflation. Average hourly wage growth slowed from 3.7% in February to 3.2% in July, while CPI inflation rose from 2.4% to 3.3% over the same stretch, nearly erasing the real-wage cushion that had been supporting household spending earlier in the year. Much of the inflation resurgence traces to the conflict in the Middle East, which drove up gasoline and energy prices.
